cards.note: Black on yellow chevrons are mainly found north of Izmir. (The yellow is somewhat orange-ish)
Around the city of Bodrum you will commonly find this type of whitewashed buildings with flat roofs, often combined with blue (or light pink) details or unpainted stone walls.

Street signs in Bursa are green, and generally have slightly extruded letters, meaning the signs are not completely flat.

  • NOTE: Several other types of infrastructure in Bursa, such as fences and guardrails, may also be coloured green.
Cotton is mainly found in the region surrounding the city of Şanlıurfa.

Four-lane divided highways with no divider, other than double middle road lines, are almost exclusively found in the eastern half of the country.

  • Beware that divided highways with clear dividers, such as guardrails, can still be found in the east.
Flat roofs are mostly found in the southeast and to a lesser extent along the south coast.
Göreme, west of Kayseri, can be recognised by the tall sandstone monoliths with ancient dwellings carved into them.

cards.a: Horizontal Tanks with Vertical Tanks Under
cards.note: Horizontal water tanks placed on top of vertical water tanks are primarily found in a line following the south coast and going up to Elâzığ.

Red street signs with a coloured bottom strip are found in several cities. In the bottom right corner, you can find a white arrow and some numbers. If this arrow is pointing in both directions and has a single arrowhead, rather than double, then you are almost certainly in Istanbul.

  • Beware that simple arrows pointing in only one direction can be found in both Istanbul and in other cities. However, if you see such signs in combination with red house numbers, then you should be in Istanbul.
Street signs in the Izmir Province are dark blue, noticeably bulge outwards and very commonly have the emblem of Izmir in white at the top of the sign.
Lake Van is by far the biggest lake in Turkey and has a semi-arid landscape, being surrounded by dry grassy hills and occasional trees and agricultural fields near the shore.

Metal roofs are most common in the east.

  • Note that for this and the other roof-related tips to be reliable, the majority of all visible roofs should preferably be of that type.

Mount Ararat, labelled as Ağrı Dağı on Google Maps, is a dormant volcano in far eastern Turkey and the tallest mountain in the country. It is often seen together with Küçük Ağrı, a smaller volcano to the southeast.
Many buildings in the Nevşehir Province are built by large, light and unevenly coloured, sandstone bricks.

In the northeast you will find uncultivated grasslands in valleys surrounded by round hills. Trees are very limited in the region. In Generation 3 the area has an extremely distinct look, with deep green grass covering the hills. It is significantly more difficult to recognise in Generation 4, where the grass has a more arid look.

Some of the new Gen 4 truck coverage is greener since it was also taken in the spring.
Olive trees are mainly found on the Mediterranean coast.
Turkish area codes follow a fairly easy to learn pattern and can be very useful to get the general region. Most notably, the first digit of area codes are ordered from 2 in the west to 4 in the east.
Sheet metal roofs shaped like low pyramids are mainly found far east, particularly in the general area surrounding Lake Van.
River valleys surrounded by steep, barren and rocky cliff sides can be found between the cities of Erzurum and Artvin and in the southeast near the city of Hakkâri.
This Road with extreme fog and yellow lines can be seen southeast of Izmit.
White spherical water tanks can be found in the southeast, mainly south of Batman.
Square water tanks with angled corners are found in the south, approximately from İskenderun to Sanliurfa.

Street signs in the Ankara Province are blue with a small round top. Similar street signs can very rarely be found in Giresun.

Beware that some newer street signs are red.
Sunflowers are mainly found in northwestern Turkey.
Tea plantations are common in the province of Rize

Tiled roofs are mostly found in the western two thirds of the country.

  • Note that for this and the other roof-related tips to be reliable, the majority of all visible roofs should preferably be of that type.
If you find yourself surrounded by greenhouses, you are likely to be along the south coast west of Adana.

Turkish pines (pinus brutia) are mainly found near the Mediterranean coast.

  • NOTE: Turkish pines can appear very similar to Aleppo pines, which are uncommon in Turkey, but are often found in other Mediterranean countries.
A majority of all vineyards in Turkey can be found in a region east of Izmir.
Dark, volcanic rocks are commonly found between the cities of Şanlıurfa and Diyarbakır.
Yellow on black chevrons are mainly found in and around the Balıkesir Province in the west and in the Kars Province in the far east. Beware that you may very rarely find them elsewhere.
